role.altitude: The driver's week is still the round, the cab and the deliveries. Less of it is retyping the log, the cargo list and the card total on the cash sheet. The cash count, the hand-in, the paper note and the radio call stay at full length.
reach: Dispatchers and the base: the hours check and the delay note, the same day
Depot cashiers: the counted cash and the receipts, once, at the end of the round
skills_to_grow: Read a remaining-driving-time figure and still decide to stop
Count a short bag before it is handed in
Say on the radio whether people are hurt, not only that the road is blocked
role.ambitious_version: At the end of the round the log, the cargo list and the card totals are already on one sheet. The driver still counts the cash, still holds a paper note when the rules require one, and still makes the radio call.

tasks.short: Vehicle logs, cargo records and billing statements

steps.what: Maintain vehicle logs from the tachograph download rather than a pad.
Keep cargo records from the delivery scan on the day sheet.
Read tachograph remaining time in accordance with the driving-time regulations.
Draft billing statements from the delivered stops already recorded.
Hold the paper cargo note that the regulations still require.

tasks.design: The {OTHER} tachograph download replaces the pad for the vehicle log, and the driver only confirms the day is theirs. Cargo records come from the delivery scan on the {OPS_SYSTEM}, made when the goods are handed over, and the driver reviews lines that do not match. Billing statements are drafted in the {SPREADSHEET} from stops already recorded, and a paper note the rules still require is filed in {DOCS} in full.
tasks.previous_blocker: The log, the cargo list and the billing lines lived on paper in the cab, so the same facts were written twice.
tasks.enabler_now: A tachograph download and a delivery scan already exist in ordinary transport software, and an electronic consignment note can be issued inside that system.
tasks.still_hard: A paper note from a foreign shipper, a driving-time judgement at the roadside, and a billing dispute.
tasks.human_edge: The driver knows whether the download is their own day, whether a short cargo line is a real miss, and when to stop for the break.

ambition.what: Catch a driving-time breach or a cargo mismatch the same day, because the log and the scan are already on the sheet.

tasks.altitude: The hours check and a paper note stay. The pad is no longer retyped.

reach.learn: Which mismatch is a real miss, and which remaining-time figure means the driver must stop.
The driver's list is a draft of delivered stops, not the issued bill.

evidence.claim: An electronic consignment note can be created, issued and signed inside the transport system, so cargo fields need not be retyped.
A tachograph record can be downloaded and archived remotely, and the same tool raises a remaining-driving-time alert.
Driving time is limited to 9 hours a day, 10 hours twice a week, 56 hours a week and 90 hours in two weeks, with a 45-minute break after 4.5 hours, checked from tachograph records.
From 1 July 2026, vans of 2.5 to 3.5 tonnes in paid international transport need a tachograph. A domestic light round may sit outside that rule.
Authorities must accept certified electronic freight data from 9 July 2027, but abroad a driver may still need a paper note.
Telematics and a driver app observe location and behaviour, and works-council consent covers that observation.
A log of hours and cargo is not scoring a driver or allocating work by behaviour. That scoring rule applies from 2 December 2027.
Scanner indicators of exact idle time, kept 31 days, drew a fine of 32 million euro in December 2023. A trip log must not become that kind of score, and the fine is not a measure of time saved.
No digest source measures this driver's minutes on the pad, so the split between copying and checking is a judgement.

assumptions: The prior puts 50 percent on meetings in person. That time is the driver filling paper in the cab, not a meeting. The log copy and the cargo copy are s1 and s2, and those are the steps that shrink.
The hours check stays at 70 percent of today's step because the driver still decides to stop. The paper note stays at 100 percent. No step is reduced to zero, and there is no model loop.

Structured inputs: the tachograph produces driver identity, day start and driving minutes during the drive. If the download fails, the driver copies those three fields from the card display, and that fallback is the remaining time on s1. The delivery scan produces stop, quantity and signature status when the goods are handed over, on the delivery task, which is not this task. This task only used to copy that scan. If a stop has no scan, the driver keeps the paper note and types the line. Prices on the billing draft come from the office price list. The office posts the customer bill. No second signature exists on this task.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours is one missed cargo or billing line corrected after the first review. It is not the build, and it is not the paper filing already counted on s5.

An office case about invoice lead time is not this role and is not used as time saved. Telematics here are hours and trip facts, not a behaviour score. Whether consent for location tracking already exists is an unknown.
unknowns: Whether this fleet's vans are in paid international transport above 2.5 tonnes.
Whether works-council consent for the driver app and the tachograph download already exists.
Whether the driver or the office issues the customer bill.
research_questions: Which stops still arrive with a paper consignment note, and does the driver or the office raise the bill?

already_counted.description: Confirm the downloaded vehicle log is the driver's own day.
Read a cargo line that does not match the stop.
Decide whether to stop from the tachograph remaining-time figure.
Check the billing draft against the delivered stops.
File the paper cargo note the rules still require.

incremental.description: Correct one cargo or billing line the first review missed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A domestic day where the tachograph download and the delivery scan already exist saves the retyping of the log and the cargo list. A day with a paper note from a foreign shipper and a billing dispute keeps the check and the paper filing at full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Sort the receipts and the cash taken on deliveries.
Count the money received against the day's delivery notes.
Turn the counted money and the receipts in at the depot.
Write only the received cash figure; the point-of-sale already holds the card total.
File the receipts signed for those deliveries.

tasks.design: Sorting the cash, counting it and walking it to the depot stay as they are. The only shorter step is the cash sheet in {DOCS}: the {OTHER} point-of-sale already holds the card total, so the driver writes the received cash figure and not the card slips. The count gates the hand-in.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash, card slips and paper receipts arrived as one pile, and the total was added by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: The point-of-sale already has the card total for the round.
tasks.still_hard: The notes and the coins still have to be counted, and the bag still has to be walked in.
tasks.human_edge: The driver is the person who took the money and can say which drop was short.

ambition.what: Spot a short drop the same evening, because the card total is already on the sheet and only the cash figure is new.

tasks.altitude: The count and the hand-in stay at full length. The card totals are not added by hand.

reach.learn: The driver's count is the version handed in, and a short bag is named before it leaves the driver.

evidence.claim: No digest source times a driver's cash hand-in, so the split between counting and the cash sheet is a judgement.
Counting a cash bag is not scoring a driver or allocating work by behaviour. That scoring rule applies from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: The prior puts about 63 percent on meetings in person. That time is the count and the walk, not a meeting. Sorting, counting and the walk stay at remaining 100 percent because the design does not change them.

Only the cash sheet is shorter. The point-of-sale produces the card total at the moment of the card payment, on the delivery, which is not this task. If that total is missing, the driver adds the card slips by hand, which is the other half of s4. The driver writes the received cash figure beside it.

The driver is the only person in today's steps. A depot recount is other-role upkeep, not time removed from the driver's baseline. No model reads the notes. The cash leaves the driver's hands, so the hand-in is gated by the count the driver just did. No second person signs today.
Upkeep of 1 hour per 100 baseline hours is chasing one receipt that was not in the bag. It is not the build, and it is not the count or the walk already kept in full.
unknowns: Whether cash is handed to a depot cashier, dropped in a safe, or paid into a bank.
What the driver may do when the counted total does not match the notes.
research_questions: What share of this site's deliveries is still cash, and who recounts the bag?

already_counted.description: Sort the receipts and the cash before the count.
Count the money against the delivery notes.
Walk the counted bag to the depot.
Write the received cash figure beside the card total.
File the signed receipts after the hand-in.

incremental.description: Chase one receipt that was not in the bag.
Depot cashier recounts the bag after the hand-in.

approvals.approved_version: Counted cash and the day's receipts, as the driver counted them before handing them to the depot.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A day of card payments saves re-adding those totals onto the cash sheet. A day of many cash drops keeps the sort, the count and the walk at full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Delay and accident reports by radio

steps.what: See delays, accidents, or other traffic situations on the road.
Report delays using telephones or mobile radios to the bases.
Warn other vehicles when the radios reach them.
Write the transportation situation from the stop already on the round.
File the situation note where the base can read it.

tasks.design: Seeing the road, the telephone or radio call on {TELEPHONY}, and the warning to other vehicles stay at full length. The written note in {DOCS} is shorter because it starts from the stop and the time already on the round. Filing the note is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: The base number and the place had to be recalled and then written out after the call.
tasks.enabler_now: The round's stops are already on the day sheet, so the written note can start from the stop and the time.
tasks.still_hard: Whether people are hurt, and what other vehicles need to hear, is a judgement on the road.
tasks.human_edge: The driver can see the road and say whether people are hurt, which a stored list of road names cannot.
tasks.altitude: The driver still sees the road and still makes the call at full length. The written note is shorter.

reach.learn: Which situations the driver has already told other vehicles, and which the base must call onward.
The warning names whether the road is blocked and whether people are hurt.

evidence.claim: No digest source times a radio call, so almost all of this task staying with the driver is a judgement.
Storing a delay note with the vehicle's location observes the driver. Works-council consent covers telematics and a driver app.
Reporting a road hazard is not scoring the driver or allocating work by behaviour. That scoring rule applies from 2 December 2027.
A delay note must not become a score of exact idle time. Scanner indicators of that kind, kept 31 days, drew a fine of 32 million euro in December 2023.

assumptions: The prior puts 92.3 percent on meetings in person. That time is the driver seeing the road and speaking on the telephone or radio, not a sit-down meeting. Seeing, the call and the warning stay at remaining 100 percent.

Only the written note is shorter, because the stop and the time are already on the round. That stop list is produced when the round is planned, on the planning task, which is not this task. If the stop is not on the sheet, the driver writes the place from memory, which is the other half of s4. The call is not automated, and no second person approves it before it goes out.
Upkeep of 0.5 hours per 100 baseline hours is correcting a wrong location on the note after the call. It is not the build. The note records the situation, not a behaviour score and not idle time.
unknowns: Whether the base is reached by radio, by telephone, or both.
Whether an accident must also be called to the authorities by the driver or by the base.
research_questions: Which situations the driver is expected to call in, and which the base calls onward?

already_counted.description: See the delay, the accident or the other traffic situation.
Make the telephone or radio call to the base.
Warn other vehicles on the radio.
Write the situation onto the note from the planned stop.
File the situation note for the base.

incremental.description: Correct a wrong location on the written note after the call.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A known road delay saves rewriting the place on the note. An accident keeps the call at full length, so almost none of the task moves.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
